novel_features.name: Triage queue
novel_features.description: See per-agent open ticket load, stale tickets, and 24-hour SLA-breach count in one table — the dispatcher view Halo's UI scatters across five tabs.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining tickets × agents × statuses in the local SQLite store; the API only returns these one entity at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent asks 'who should I assign this P1 to' or 'where are we bleeding'. One call, one screen.

novel_features.name: Bulk age-out closer
novel_features.description: Find tickets stale in a status for N days, preview them, then bulk-close with a templated action via --apply.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQLite filter computes stale; --apply issues batch close + action through the API. No competitor offers the preview-then-apply pattern.
novel_features.example: halopsa-pp-cli tickets age-out --status "Awaiting Customer" --stale-days 14 --action-note "Auto-closing per policy" --apply
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on the Monday queue cleanse to close 30 stale tickets in one command instead of 30 clicks.

novel_features.name: SLA breach radar
novel_features.description: List tickets whose targetdate falls in the next N hours, sorted by time-to-breach, with agent + client + current status.
novel_features.rationale: Halo's UI has a breach board but no shareable filter + sort by time-to-breach across the whole team.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on Friday afternoon or anytime before a hand-off to pre-empt SLA breaches.

novel_features.name: Agent workload
novel_features.description: Per-agent: open tickets, tickets touched this week, billable hours logged, oldest open ticket age.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-joins tickets × actions × time_entries × agents in local store — no single API endpoint returns this composite.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when rebalancing the queue or asking 'who's overloaded'.

novel_features.name: Client desk card
novel_features.description: One panel: client + sites + active tickets + open contracts + contract hours remaining + recent KB articles linked to their tickets + asset count.
novel_features.rationale: Six-table cross-join in local SQLite. The defining MSP technician command — replaces four browser tabs with one printout.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on every client call. Open it before answering the phone, paste it into ticket notes.

novel_features.name: Asset ticket history
novel_features.description: Every ticket that touched this asset, chronological, with agent and time logged.
novel_features.rationale: Local join of tickets × asset_id over time; the API forces you to look at one ticket at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a machine keeps coming back to the queue — the pattern lives in the history, not in the latest ticket.

novel_features.name: KB suggest for ticket
novel_features.description: FTS5-rank KB articles against a ticket's summary + details + last action text; print top 5 with snippets.
novel_features.rationale: Local FTS5 index makes mechanical ranking fast and offline; the API has no 'similar KB' endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this mid-call when a known fix probably exists but you don't remember the exact KB title.

novel_features.name: Time gap finder
novel_features.description: List tickets the agent touched this week that have zero time logged on them.
novel_features.rationale: Set-diff between actions and time_entries — only computable when both are in the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on Friday before submitting the timesheet. Stops 'I know I worked that ticket but where is it' archaeology.

novel_features.name: Contract burn-down
novel_features.description: Per contract: hours bank, hours consumed this period (sum of billable time on that client's tickets), days remaining, projected overage.
novel_features.rationale: Three-way local aggregation (contracts × time_entries × clients); Halo's native reports cannot project overage.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this mid-month before a client conversation — know whether they're tracking over their bank.

novel_features.name: Ticket rules dump
novel_features.description: Print every ticket rule and workflow as readable flat text — conditions → actions, one block per rule.
novel_features.rationale: Halo's UI has no export; auditing rules means clicking through each one. Local table read + format.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this during quarterly automation audits or when investigating an unexpected routing.

novel_features.name: Changed-since
novel_features.description: Tickets where any action or status change occurred since timestamp, grouped by ticket.
novel_features.rationale: Backed by incremental sync; replaces brittle homegrown PowerShell ETLs that break on field changes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this after a meeting or when coming back from lunch. 'What did I miss' in one call.

novel_features.name: Standup digest
novel_features.description: Per-agent for the window: tickets closed, tickets reopened, time logged, top client.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregation across tickets + actions + time_entries; no Halo report gives this shape exactly.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this the moment before standup. One paste, everyone sees yesterday's progress.

novel_features.name: Multi-client overlay
novel_features.description: Rank all clients by a chosen metric (open tickets, stale, SLA at-risk, hours over bank). Top N out.
novel_features.rationale: Exploits the defining MSP shape — many clients in one tenant. Local rank, pluggable metric.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when looking for the next escalation to invest time in. Whichever client is on top is the one to call.

narrative.headline: Every HaloPSA, HaloITSM and HaloCRM feature, plus a local SQLite store and cross-entity views the API can't return.
narrative.value_prop: Wraps the full Halo REST API (952 endpoints across tickets, clients, assets, contracts, time, KB, and workflows) with offline-first search, agent-native JSON output, and cross-entity commands like `triage`, `client card`, and `contracts burn` that join tables Halo's UI scatters across five tabs.
narrative.auth_narrative: Halo uses OAuth2 client_credentials. Create an API application in your tenant under Configuration > Integrations > Halo PSA API (Authentication Method: Client ID and Secret — Services), then run `halopsa-pp-cli auth login --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret> --tenant <yoursub>`. The CLI exchanges the credentials at https://<tenant>.halopsa.com/auth/token and caches the access token (auto-refreshed before expiry).

quickstart.comment: Confirm setup. Set HALOPSA_TENANT, HALOPSA_CLIENT_ID, and HALOPSA_CLIENT_SECRET in your env first (or run `halopsa-pp-cli auth login` for an interactive prompt); doctor verifies the token mints and a sample GET succeeds.
First sync pulls tickets, clients, sites, agents, assets, contracts, KB into the local SQLite store
The dispatcher view — per-agent load, stale count, 24h breach count in one table
The keystone command — client + sites + tickets + contracts + assets + KB in one panel

quickstart.command: halopsa-pp-cli sql "SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM tickets WHERE assigned_team='Support' GROUP BY status"
quickstart.comment: Drop into SQL when the prebuilt commands don't fit

troubleshoots.fix: Run `halopsa-pp-cli doctor` — the token may have expired or your client_id lost the required scopes. Re-run `auth login`.

troubleshoots.symptom: Empty list results that should have data
troubleshoots.fix: Pass `--include-inactive` (clients/users) or `--include-deleted` (tickets) — Halo filters these by default. Verify with `halopsa-pp-cli sql "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets"`.
Initial sync pulls all 952 endpoints' top resources. Subsequent `sync` runs use `lastupdatedfrom` and are fast. Use `--only tickets,clients` to scope.

troubleshoots.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests during a burst
troubleshoots.fix: The client auto-retries with exponential backoff. If it persists, lower `--concurrency` (default 4) on batch commands.
Confirm your Halo subdomain at https://<tenant>.halopsa.com (or .haloitsm.com / .halocrm.com). Pass `--tenant-domain haloitsm.com` to override the default `.halopsa.com`.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for halopsa-pp-cli when an agent needs to triage, dispatch, or report against a HaloPSA / HaloITSM / HaloCRM tenant without clicking through the web UI. It is the right tool for cross-entity questions ("who's overloaded", "which tickets are about to breach", "which client is burning their contract"), bulk operations (stale-ticket close, batch action posts, batch time entries), and ETLs that previously required hand-rolled scripts. It is NOT the right tool for end-user portal browsing or for tenants you don't have API credentials to.

recipes.command: halopsa-pp-cli tickets age-out --status "Awaiting Customer Reply" --stale-days 14 --action-note "Auto-closing per policy"
recipes.explanation: Preview every stale customer-waiting ticket. Add --apply when you're ready to close them.

recipes.title: Friday SLA radar before hand-off
recipes.explanation: List every ticket the on-call shift inherits that's at risk of breaching SLA in their first 24h. Pipe to anything.

recipes.title: Pre-call client briefing
recipes.explanation: Get the client's complete situation in one query before answering the phone. Use --select to narrow what an agent sees.

recipes.title: Friday timesheet reconcile
recipes.explanation: Find every ticket you touched this week with zero time logged so the gap doesn't ship with your timesheet.

recipes.title: Contract overage check before client meeting
recipes.explanation: See current hours consumed vs. bank with projected overage so the contract conversation isn't a surprise.
